requirements.requirement: The system must render a 'clean' malpractice state when backend status is clean and display the corresponding visual indicator.
The system must render a 'flagged' malpractice state when backend status is flagged and display the corresponding visual indicator.
The system must render an 'unknown' malpractice state when backend status is null or missing.
The system must display a valid, clickable state_board_url when provided in the backend response.
The system must not render a state board link when state_board_url is missing or invalid.
The system must correctly display the malpractice score_contribution value as provided by the backend without mutation.
The system must include the malpractice measure in the overall provider scorecard rendering output.
The system must not include prohibited terms such as 'fraud' or 'misconduct' in any malpractice-related UI text.
The system must render malpractice messaging using neutral, signal-only language across all display states.
The system must produce consistent UI snapshots for identical malpractice input data across test runs.
The system must fail tests when rendered malpractice text deviates from approved wording patterns.
The system must correctly render malpractice UI when case_count and last_incident_date are present.
The system must gracefully omit optional fields when case_count and last_incident_date are absent without breaking layout.
The system must pass end-to-end tests validating full data flow from API response through rendering pipeline to UI output.
The system must fail end-to-end tests when backend returns malformed malpractice data structures.
The system must ensure all rendered malpractice content is compatible with MessageBubble.tsx markdown-safe rendering.
The system must verify that no raw HTML or unsafe links are rendered within the malpractice section.
The system must validate that flagged state rendering includes a visible distinction from clean state in UI snapshots.
The system must ensure that neutral malpractice language does not imply legal judgment or wrongdoing.
The system must validate that all malpractice-related UI strings conform to predefined approved text patterns for consistency.
